doc.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009

title: Musical family and family quartet
summary: His parents and brother were musical; the family sang four-part harmony and he learned uke and guitar.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You are a musical family situation?

Yes. My father played the banjo and the piano in college and wrote, actually wrote the first Tau Kappa Epsilon sweetheart song. All the fraternities had sweetheart songs. And so he wrote that and played ukulele too I guess. And then my mother sang alto in church choirs and gave piano lessons and they met in Florida because my father was soloing in a church on Sunday. And so they married and then my brother was born in ’28 and I was

born in ’36 and we moved up north. And my brother was musical, had a great voice, played the trombone and the drums, and so when I came along I learned to play the ukulele and then the guitar. We ended up with a family quartet with four part harmony. And I usually did the chording and sang the melody and my brother would do the bass and my dad would do the high tenor and my mother would do the second tenor. And I learned harmony in a way from that. It was great fun.

Yes. Yes. So we did a lot of sitting on the front porch singing songs. And then when I was in high school I was asked frequently to lead sing-a-longs for the boarding students at the school I went to on Sundays, and then we’d just get together in some common room and I’d play the ukulele.
